text_fidelity_a:
Graphite Pickleball Paddles Set of 4, 2023 USAPA Approved, Carbon Fiber Surface (CHS), Polypropylene Lightweight Honeycomb Core, 3 Indoor 3 Outdoor Pickleball, 4 Replacement Soft Grip + Bag I like that this comes with its own little zippered carrying case. That's just an extra that makes it nicer than having to find a duffel-bag or some other place to carry the set.

It comes with 4 paddles that are the same except for the colors. It has 3 indoor and 3 outdoor balls which are almost identical except for the spacing of the holes. They're like Whiffle™ balls. The holes prevent them from going too far from the air resistance. The ones for indoors are the ones with the bigger holes because you can't hit them as far.

I know it says that you can play indoors and technically that's true, but it depends on where you're playing. A big game room with lots of space would work. A place where you can trip over furniture or knock over lamps isn't a good idea. It also depends on how aggressive you want to be with your swings. The indoor balls are not the problem because they couldn't easily build up enough momentum to break anything except very delicate or top-heavy things. But the paddles swinging around are more of the issue with playing indoors. A big swing or stretch if you aren't aware of the stuff around you could be where you'd break something or trip over something. But still, about the same level of caution you'd have with Ping-Pong, but without the table to keep you in place.

The paddles are pretty nice quality and lighter than they look like they should be. But they have a lot of surface area and the balls are easier to hit than with Ping-Pong paddles.

You'll have to look up the rules online because they aren't included, but really that's only if you want to play "official Pickle-ball". You can play it with Ping-pong rules, badminton rules, volleyball rules, tennis rules -- just about any of the similar kind of games that I can think of -- it's just a bit easier and has requires less skill or movement. It's really about the same level of activity that you'd have with badminton and the same sized area if you're playing outdoors.

Personally, indoors is just if we want to play "hit-the-ball-back-and-forth-down-the-hallway" because it's too hot/cold/wet outside.

This doesn't come with a net, and I thought the rubberband strips might have been to map out the court area, but it's supposed to be for the grip on the paddles. If you're going to play "official" you'll need a net which is pretty much the same as a badminton net just not as high. It's basically a mini tennis court with much the same net.

It's good exercise, and I can't imagine this being a competitive sport, but I was wrong about tag being an 'official' sport when I heard someone mention it -- but it actually is and surprisingly fun to watch -- with sponsors and everything. Pickleball might be the same because why wouldn't someone take something that's fun and add a bunch of rules so they can make some money from advertising.

It's good for staying active and just about everyone likes to play because we don't play with any real rules. Not because we have odd ideas like "there are no losers here", but because it's just that unimportant.

I can't comment on the price with the way things are these days, but it seems to be about the same price as other options, and the quality is decent. The bag is a bonus and even the dog likes to play -- but that's where it goes from being 'pickle-ball' to 'slobber-ball'.

Overall, this is a nice set, especially the paddles. Five stars.
text_fidelity_b: Graphite Pickleball Paddles Set of 4, 2023 USAPA Approved, Carbon Fiber Surface (CHS), Polypropylene Lightweight Honeycomb Core, 3 Indoor 3 Outdoor Pickleball, 4 Replacement Soft Grip + Bag

text_fidelity_a:
Coleman Montana Camping Tent, 6/8 Person Family Tent with Included Rainfly, Carry Bag, and Spacious Interior, Fits Multiple Queen Airbeds and Sets Up in 15 Minutes As an adult who has just recently returned to the world of camping (I am a leader in my son's cub scout pack), I looked at LOTS of tent options before choosing the Coleman Montana 8 person tent. I checked out reviews on Amazon and CampMor, and talked to as many camping enthusiast friends as I could. My first year in scouting, I borrowed a Eureka 2-person tent from our local boy scout troop, which came up to (maybe) my waist, and just barely fit my full-sized air mattress. After struggling to change clothing while lying down (I could barely kneel, let alone stand), and suffering through a fairly sleepless/stuffy night in the Eureka tent, I decided that the following features were necessary for comfortable camping:

1. The ability to stand up fully. This meant that any tent I chose had to have a center height of at least 72", preferably more (my husband is 6 feet tall, and if I ever want him to join us camping, the tent needs to work for him too. The Montana 8 has a center height of 84" (7 feet).

2. Room for gear and at least two full/queen sized air mattresses. Although the Montana 8 states that there's room for 8 people, the diagram shows these 8 people sleeping in mummy bags very close together. From a comfort perspective, this tent will hold 4-5 people (and their gear) at a maximum, without feeling overly crowded. For the three of us, this fits the bill nicely.

3. Intuitive and easy to set up and take down. While I like camping, I am not an avid camper. Finding a tent that can be set up (and taken down) with only help from a 9 year old was key, and this fits the bill nicely.

4. Good cross-ventilation. After sleeping in a stuffy tent once, I didn't want to repeat the experience. Three windows (the two side windows and the door window) can be rolled down to allow for good air flow and ventilation. We rolled the windows down 1/3 of the way, which provided a very comfortable cross-breeze while sleeping.

5. Waterproof with a bathtub floor. Many of the reviewers stated that they had no problems with leaks along the seams without using any waterproofing sealant. After talking with others and reading some recommendations, I used the Kiwi Camp Dry Heavy Duty Water Repellent to spray the seams prior to our first use, as added protection. We had some light rain during the evening, and much heavier rain the next morning, and the inside of the tent stayed bone dry.

6. Quality. I wanted a tent that would stand up to occasional car camping trips, without having to be replaced on a regular basis. Coleman is a recognized brand, and after talking with folks who own Coleman tents and reading the reviews, I was convinced that this tent would be a good one for our family. So far, I'm pleased!

6. Price. Given that we don't do a lot of camping, I didn't want to spend hundreds on a tent. I purchased the Montana 8 in Blue (not the Elite) from Amazon in mid-May 2015, and paid $136.48; a surprisingly low price for this particular tent model/size.

Some nice features that this tent offers (that weren't on my list of must-haves):

1. A port for electrical/extension cords. While this tent does not have electricity, it does include a port near the door that allows campers to run an extension cord into the tent (for use with lanterns, fans, etc.)

2. A covered entry area. I looked at tents that had screened in areas, but opted for this one instead, choosing to have the extra room inside the tent rather than in a screened area. I had two camp chairs outside - in the evening, when it started to rain, I placed the camp chairs under the front rain fly "awning", on either side of the door. Despite the rain, the chairs stayed mostly dry, with only a few drops of water on them.

3. A "D door". This door has a pole that threads around the D curve, and another one at the hinge axis, which means that the door can function as a real door in terms of opening/closing, rather than a door that must be zipped open and closed. While there are Velcro closures around the D curve, we found that to keep insects from getting in we still had to zip it shut. However, we liked the easy entry!

All in all, my family and I are very pleased with our new tent, and look forward to many years of use!
text_fidelity_b: Coleman Montana Camping Tent, 6/8 Person Family Tent with Included Rainfly, Carry Bag, and Spacious Interior, Fits Multiple Queen Airbeds and Sets Up in 15 Minutes

text_fidelity_a: Grabber Outdoors Stainless Steel Adjustable Pocket Stove With 8 Fuel Tabs For many years, I've used Esbit / hexamine fuel tabs with a similar folding stove.  It's not my primary heat source, but rather I use it for times I need a little quick fire, or to get larger fires started.  One tab is enough to get 2 cups of water boiling, in most weather conditions.  The stove works fairly well with most mess kit items.  But, I more regularly use parts of a tab as tinder to get larger sticks going, so I build a bigger fire.  I can cook larger things on the large fire, and then I'll move some coals to the folding stove to heat up smaller items, or put hot rocks into it for portable heat.  The stove isn't all that rugged, but it holds up better than my improvised soda can stoves, and packs up very nicely (you can fit 4 tabs in the stove when it's folded).  I've also used trioxane, but the Esbit / hexamine tabs burn cleaner and hotter for longer, and are easier to find deals on.  For casual trips, where I don't need a big fire, don't carry any kind of gas fuel, sticks may not be plentiful, or I just need to heat up some coffee or a freeze dried meal - the combination of this stove, one hexamine tab and a steel cup works perfectly for me.  At such a low price, I won't feel guilty using up the tabs, or if the stove gets a little beat up.

Coleman Camping Tent with Instant Setup, 4/6/8/10 Person Weatherproof Tent with Integrated Rainfly, Double-Thick Fabric, and Included Carry Bag, Sets Up in 60 Seconds I've had this for about 3 years now, and I really do enjoy it. This is the go-to car-camping brought-way-too-much-stuff tent for fine weather. My husband likes it because he doesn't have to crawl to get around in it. I love that I can get it up in a few minutes without help. It's roomy and comfortable, but there are caveats.

-This is a single-layer tent without a rain fly. You can't leave the windows open in damp weather, and you WILL get tons of condensation in wet or cool conditions. It hasn't leaked badly in the rain for me, except when the rain has blown through the top vents. Keep your things away from the sides if you don't want them wet.

-I absolutely don't trust this thing in stormy or windy weather. It's just way too high profile for that sort of thing.

-It's bulky. I can easily fit it into the bag it came in (without needing to open the expander), but it's still large and heavy for a tent of these dimensions.

In short, this is a nice tent for a weekend with a fine weather forecast. It's not a tent for when you're going to be hours from civilization for longer than you can trust a weather forecast. Get yourself something low-slung with a fly that goes to the ground for that kind of camping.
text_fidelity_b: Coleman Camping Tent with Instant Setup, 4/6/8/10 Person Weatherproof Tent with Integrated Rainfly, Double-Thick Fabric, and Included Carry Bag, Sets Up in 60 Seconds

It's a good uphill cardio workout, strengthens the quads and glutes and helps get rid of some of those extra butt-cheeks. Dead On Tools DO-300 Killer Chiller Mobile Cooler/Lunch box, Black I bought this for my husband who works outside and needed something to keep lunch plus multiple drinks cold all day.
PROS:
- Very large size - can hold 2 larger-sized gatorade drinks PLUS a 16.9 oz water bottle in the bottom compartment with an ice pack, and 2 sandwiches with 2 16.9 oz water bottles or more on top
- Very sturdy material - thick, tear resistant, very durable
- Comes with optional shoulder strap that fits perfectly in the front zippered compartment if you need to be hands free
- Looks more masculine than LL Bean-type of lunch bags so hubby actually uses it
- Front pocket is see through mesh and perfect to hold strap and a "tick key" tick remover for outdoor use
- At under 20 bucks, it's a real bargain! I bought an extra one and put it away for when this one bites the dust

CONS:
- Black color means it gets hot outdoors or in the car - especially if the sun hits it
- White interior shows every bit of dirt (although cleans up easily with a little baking soda-water paste on a sponge)
- Zippers are sturdy, but get "stuck" quite often
- Sides are soft so will the bag will sit lop-sided if unequal size items are placed in the bottom
- Triangular shaped top (with above mentioned soft sides) makes it so things on top are easily crushed
- Top handles are too small too fit a large sized wrist through so it must be carried by hand or shoulder strap

All in all a good lunch box for men (and women) who carry lots of food and drinks for lunch. I wish there were other color options- maybe an army green or tan- so it didn't get so hot in the sun. Would also be better if at least the bottom compartment had stiff sides. Also, a zippered pouch or compartment to hold a cold pack would be nice, so it didn't have to get mixed in with contents.

It's really hard to find a durable, masculine lunch box for guys who get dirty at work or work outdoors. I've looked for something decent for years and the selection is extremely limited. This fits the bill and is very reasonably priced. For under 20 bucks, you can't do any better than this!
text_fidelity_b: Dead On Tools DO-300 Killer Chiller Mobile Cooler/Lunch box, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Eco Vessel Summit Discontinued 2014 Insulated Stainless Steel Water Bottle with Flip Straw (17-Ounce, Blue Glow) I really loved these bottles at first, so much so that I bought 8 of them. They keep my water very cold for a long, long time and I like the lids (I use them without the straws). I can hook them onto whatever I need to help me carry them, as well.

Unfortunately, my love affair with these bottles has ended all too soon. The first thing I noticed is that the paint started coming off. The red one is the worst. The paint is flaking off to the point that it would be better off if I pull the rest of it off to turn it silver instead of blotched red. But I could have lived with that.

What got me was when I started to fill one up only to discover that the plastic ring around the top of the bottle that you use to screw the lid in has split. It split completely down. There was nothing I could do. It had to either go back to the manufacturer or the trash. Since I'm a grad student, the last thing I have is extra time so I put it in the trash.

I started checking my other bottles and discovered that the plastic ring was put on at a tilt on some of the bottles (based on the amount of space under the ring not being uniform on all bottles).

Then I looked at my other bottles and noticed that the Hydro Flask's ring was metal, not plastic. I like those bottles just as much, but had to buy the straw lids separately. However, now that I see the flaw in the Eco Vessel bottles, I'm going to start replacing them with the Hydro Flask brand. Not only are they completely metal (except the lid, of course), but the finish does not show signs that it will flake off.

All in all, the plastic ring used to screw the lid onto the bottle is a fatal flaw for these bottles.

UPDATE: I added pictures showing the paint flaking off and the warped plastic at the top. I did not take pictures of the one that broke, but I thought showing one that's not broken yet, but clearly warped, might be helpful.
text_fidelity_b: Eco Vessel Summit Discontinued 2014 Insulated Stainless Steel Water Bottle with Flip Straw (17-Ounce, Blue Glow)

Malker Bicycle Light Front and Rear Silicone LED Bike Light Set - Bike Headlight and Taillight,Waterproof & Safety Road,Mountain Bike Lights,Batteries Included,4 Pack(2pcs White and 2pcs Red Light) These lights dont attach very securely to some places where I would like to put them. The batteries dont last very long and its a pain to replace them. Each light needs two batteries so buy plenty of spares. Spares are cheap enough if you shop on Amazon. I would not buy expensive spare batteries because odds are the batteries are going to be used up when I forget to turn the lights off.

Im amending this review after I was contacted by the seller with an offer to replace the lights or give me a refund. That level of customer service deserves mention. I have also had more experience using these lights since I originally wrote the review.

I decided to keep the lights.

I had problems finding places to attach them to my beach cruiser mostly because I have a lot of baskets and a rear rack on the bike. I frequently have my gym bag, or other stuff, on the rear rack so attaching to the seat post is not an option for me if I want good visibility from behind.

The other night my partner and I rode our bikes to the movies. We knew it was going to be dark when we got out. He had never ridden his bike at night so he has no lights on it. I took a couple of these lights in my pocket and attached them to his hybrid bike before we started home in the dark. They attached fine to the seat post and handle bars on his bike and provided a lot of visibility for our ride home.

I decided to just keep these lights and carry them as spares when I ride at night. Its hard to predict when my rechargeable lights will die and having a couple of spares with me will let me show enough light in a pinch. I figured out I can attach one of the red ones through the slots in my helmet so I can get my rear light clear of the stuff Im carrying on the rear rack.

These lights are fine for occasional use or to serve as backups to larger lights. Most people will find them serviceable in a pinch and certainly way better than no light.

You should look at these lights as a way to increase your visibility at night. The white light is not powerful enough to illuminate your path but in the strobe mode does make you visible.
text_fidelity_b: Malker Bicycle Light Front and Rear Silicone LED Bike Light Set - Bike Headlight and Taillight,Waterproof & Safety Road,Mountain Bike Lights,Batteries Included,4 Pack(2pcs White and 2pcs Red Light)

text_fidelity_a:
Minn Kota Endura C2 30 Freshwater Transom Mounted Trolling Motor (30" Shaft) What I meant by the catchy headline is that this is about the minimum horsepower for the small boat application. In my case I have it hooked to a Sun Dolphin 8.5 play boat. My calculation was that more power was not only not needed, but not wanted. I need those lower speeds for trolling and such. Also I need to make sure that when I go out I can get back in, less paddle.

Here is the deal. The thing is NOT a power hog. As of this writing (super rainy wet year) I have battled winds and currents in our overflowing rivers and having to stay on it all the time has been the test. I haven't got back to the pull out with less than a half battery yet.

My notion is that if you have a 14ft boat or less this engine is adequate. No need to break the bank if you're on a budget. For my purposes it is perfect!

The gadget that tilts the thing. Over the years I have fought with those releases. Not so on the MinnKota Endura Transom Mount Trolling Motor. Smoothest one I have ever seen.

The one thing that is not perfect is the reverse. Don't plan on running it from the front of the boat in reverse. Ain't happening. I don't know if the blades aren't pitched right or what, but the reverse really froths the water without giving much ooomph. I mean, it will back you out of the shallows, but it's not for full time use. Forward, on the other hand works just like you like.

About the handle.... Well, I wound up putting my trolling motor in the back and I was kinda worried about steering. You know, twisting around and all. But with the extension handle which you can pull out a lot or a little....it ended up being zero problem. I think I might actually like it more better on the aft now.

And one heads up. If you plan on putting a transducer onto the foot...be advised, it probably won't fit as the foot is too short. However...my workaround was to put my transducer all the way to the rear against the fin and shim it with some rubber pads on an edge so that I got it near to vertical. And my depth finder works just fine. So no harm done. You could use most anything that won't rot. Your wife's Tupperware, for instance.

I like my MinnKota Endura Transom Mount Trolling Motor a LOT and you will too. If your boat be smaller grab one. You'll be thankin' me!
text_fidelity_b: Minn Kota Endura C2 30 Freshwater Transom Mounted Trolling Motor (30" Shaft)

Duluth Pack Duluth Minn Everyday Travel Gym Market Duffle Bag Pack | Gym Sports Bag Airplane Luggage Carry-On Bag - Brown I haven't had this gym duffel for very long, but since there aren't any reviews yet I figured I should offer one. This is the most money I've ever spent on a gym bag, but I took the plunge for various reasons. One being that my last two gym bags fell apart after a few years and this bag comes with a lifetime guarantee. And boy- after receiving it and feeling the nice thickness of the canvas and just how well made this thing is I must say that I definitely see this bag being able to go through hell and back for a lifetime without ever needing replacement.

Another reason I got it was for the separate base compartment in the bottom. I had a gym bag of lesser quality that had this and honestly I don't understand why more bags don't have it. It's a fantastic extra- because it keeps things completely separated from the rest of the bag. Some might say- Well, LOTS of bags have a separate compartment to put your shoes or whatever in... but I say no. Almost all bags their seperate compartments are designed in such a way that they actually take up space in the regular compartment of the bag. When you have a gym bag that has a pocket on the sides (like most do) once you fill it, the main compartment of the bag now has less space because the bulge is moving into the main compartment area. But bags with a base compartment like this one don't have this problem. You can fill the bottom compartment up without it getting in the way of anything you might have to reach for in the main compartment and without compromising any of its inside space. Really convenient. When I go to martial Arts class I can put my uniform and pads in the base compartment without ever having to deal with them throughout the day when I'm rummaging through the main compartment looking for basic things like my wallet etc. The full measurement of the bag is about 12" high/14"wide/11"deep (I did not have the bag filled up while measuring so my estimate might be slightly off) It has leather detailing on the handles for extra comfort. Duluth Pack has an even larger bag similar to this one made large enough to fit tall boots in the base compartment. I think it's called the Duluth boot duffel. That one was too large for my needs, but it might be ideal for those who need to carry more equipment.

Made in the USA... finally something NOT made in China. Excellent quality. Thick strong Zippers that do not look like they could ever break, that also zip easily. Comes with a lifetime guarantee.

-The powdered potatoes re-hydrated well and didn’t taste too bad. They are very palatable and the texture was fine.

EUROBIKE G7 Folding Mountain Bike,27.5 Inch Full Suspension Mountain Bike for Men,21 Speeds Mens and Womens Mountain Bicycle,Dual Disc Brake Adult Foldable Bike I could be four stars...
I was looking for a foldable bike to put in a car trunk. Other similar bikes, just half the price, are all shipped from china with 2-3 month wait time with no reviews or 2-3 reviews with 5 stars. Granted they all are made in the same shop from the same chinesium but this one has 30+ positive and was delivered in 4 days.
The good. Frame is steal and well welded and painted. Its heavy but sturdy. Front fork is just as good but has a little play in the springs, not critical. Rear suspension is good enough. Rims are straight.
The so-so. I am 5-11 and set the seat is almost as high as it gets. The handle bar could be higher at my preference.
The bad. Worst thing - the brake disks mounting. Front wheel all six and four on the rear wheel had broken threads. This is a major screwup as the wheels are all aluminum and the only way to fix it is to thread next size 6mm threads. Techicaly, easy fix but this should never happen! Next - the shifters are the cheapest i have seen. The left 3-grear broke while adjusting it. The push lever was grinding the base that caused the latch pin to deflect. I expected to replace them anyhow so it wasnt a show stopper.
And the special thing - the hand pump. This bike comes with a hand pump. I dont know what happened to it, either a $1-per hour laborer or rats on the container ship, either one is a shame for a bike with this price tag, but the pump was all chewed up. Dont believe me - see the pictures
So, two things, the disk brake screws and shifter - two stars,
I would not recommend this bike but there are not too many alternatives. Well, unless you are willing to take the risk and order one from china with no reviews.

I would not describe these as being soft or cozy. These are targeted at being travel blankets that should stay cleaner and drier for longer. A negative to this material is that it blocks moisture from escaping, so you can end up sweaty, especially if you are sleeping in a car without any airflow. This stores nicely in a case that can be used as a pillow. I got both the down and down alternative blankets. The down alternative blanket is thinner due to less filler material used. Both are sufficiently warm. The down alternative version should be more resistant to accumulating allergens. The down version offers more padding if you are lying down on this. Neither version offers significant padding if you are lying down on these as the filler is not dense enough to support body weight. The 45 x 80 size is enough to cover one adult unless you are obese. I washed both in a washing machine, and they came out fine.

My sleeping bag is made out of the same material on one side, and has more comfortable cotton on the inner side, with significantly more filling. It can completely unzip to use as a blanket. Depending on the scenario, a sleeping bag can be more versatile, although it takes up more room and is not designed to be used alternatively as a pillow.

GERBER Folding Spade w/Sheath - Model 5940 The Gerber folding shovel is really top notch. Its quality construction is much like any other Gerber/Fiskars equipment I've owned - it doesn't disappoint.

The shovel I have is actually a little more agressively pointed than in the pictures, so I'm not sure if Gerber has addressed this as an issue or if the pictures were off.

The top of the handle is high density polycarbonate plastic and has a horizontal design like a spade should have. You can still use the verticle part of the steel handle if you wish, but there isn't much of it. The plastic will absorb some shock compared to steel-only, and it won't freeze to your hands, etc. The polycarb handle folds down on itself, so that it actually has 3 segments (instead of several designs which have 2 segments). This means you can stow the shovel in the included cordura nylon belt pouch which is no bigger than the shovel head itself. The handle pivot point locks and since it's square, doesn't rotate or twist easily. The steel which connects the blade to the handle fits nicely inside the A angle cutout of the handle, so when collapsed it is really thin.

The blade is high quality steel with the hinged handle connected at the top. This does limit the depth of the shovel a little, but I don't believe it's much of a factor, except maybe in really solid soil where you lose a little verticle travel when the ground butts up against the hinge.

It's very compact, light, comes with a solid belt sheath (easily convertible to pack carry) and stows away easily since it's so thin. I can put it in the side pockets of my doors or in the very small space above my rear wheel well without any problems (Trailblazer 4x4).

I really can find no fault with this item, it delivers on all fronts: usability, quality, compact storage, and rugged design. I will almost certainly be keeping one in both cars and in my 72 Hour survival kit. They are even reasonably priced. 5 Stars.
text_fidelity_b: GERBER Folding Spade w/Sheath - Model 5940

text_fidelity_a:
Bearwill Golf Net, 10x7ft Heavy Duty Golf Practice Net with Golf Mat, Target Cloth, 8 Golf Tees, 6 Golf Balls, Carry Bag, Golf Training Net for Backyard Driving Chipping Indoor Outdoor Training It didn't take me long to figure out how to assemble it, even if there were no instructions. The description says this is heavy duty, and that's why I got it. Not the best golfer in the world, I wanted something that would withstand the chaos and natural disaster that constitutes my golf swing.

It comes with several soft golf balls to hit into the net. This is fine and dandy, but nothing quite replaces the feel of hitting a real, live (so to speak) golf ball. So, I broke out the real buggers and begin hitting into the net. So far, I've hit probably a thousand balls into the net. It's held up well. I leave it assembled and outside, and it's held up to the weather decently. A stiff wind WILL knock it over, however.

As to heavy duty, that's why I only gave it 4 stars. I've hit several of my typical errant shots right off the back bar brace that runs along the back of the net. It's but a nice little dent--a reminder of my burgeoning skills--complete with the golf ball dimples. Currently, I have two such dents. It seems to be holding up despite the abuse, but I expected something called "heavy duty" to withstand such impacts with a yawn and a sheepish grin. No such luck.

One of my spectacularly mishits (again using a real golf ball) hit the back bar with enough force and with the right angle that it deflected over my head and landed on the roof of my house. Hmmm. I was the one with the sheepish grin, yes sir.

I do put two bricks on the sides to keep the net firmly anchored. It does come with its own anchors, but I wasn't able to use them because the ground upon which it sits is too rocky. Not the golf net's problem. That one is my Arizona yard's personal demon. You might not have such a problem.

The hitting mat is awkward in my opinion, being so small, and unless it is anchored it will certainly move when you strike the ball, which is irritating. I even tried to anchor it, but my trench digging golf swings soon uprooted it, much to my annoyance. Also, it will raise the ball up slightly unnaturally, so you will need to find something else to stand on to make sure it is the same height as the mat. Nope, not for me. I bought a 4x5 mat that I could stand on.

Over all, I recommend this net!
text_fidelity_b: Bearwill Golf Net, 10x7ft Heavy Duty Golf Practice Net with Golf Mat, Target Cloth, 8 Golf Tees, 6 Golf Balls, Carry Bag, Golf Training Net for Backyard Driving Chipping Indoor Outdoor Training

text_fidelity_a: ESEE Authentic Model 4HM Fixed Blade Knife, Black Powder Blade, Micarta Handle, Leather Sheath I have experience with 4X ESEE knives, and there is a tool for every job - I love them all.  I bought this one to "downsize" from the ESEE Laser Strike which I found to be way too heavy to carry all day, and while a phenomenal knife, was not as well suited for smaller tasks.  This one I found to be the perfect size for just about everything you do in the outdoors.  Also, for folks with smaller hands, or a desire to work the blade more deftly, the smaller handle drops weight and is more easy to manipulate vs. it's larger cousins. After much experimentation, I've settled on carrying this knife as well as the tiny fisherman version which has a very small blade (2.5 inch) and is perfect for squirrel and fish work.  The two together cover most tasks well.  I also purchased an aftermarket fire steel with a kydex sheath which I added later. I then had to MOD the blade by ever-so-gently using an electric wire brush to remove just about an inch of the blade coating on the spine of the blade right near the handle so you can effectively spark the fire steel.  Now, that will require extra oil maintenance to prevent rust, but if you take care of your tools, they will take care of you.  I would love to see ESEE create a sheath which could house all three items (anybody listening?).  Now if you are bushcrafting, remember to always carry a folding saw (safer) or a small axe.  With those four tools, and a sharpening stone, you can rebuild civilization!  If you have never had an ESEE knife, you will love this, so don't hesitate as it is bomb proof and will last you forever.  If you could only have one blade and your life depended on it, this is the one.  I may make some videos on this knife and when I do, you can find them at "Thecameracommando" on youtube.  Cheers and happy camping!
text_fidelity_b: ESEE Authentic Model 4HM Fixed Blade Knife, Black Powder Blade, Micarta Handle, Leather Sheath

Zebco 11 Micro Fishing Fishing Reel I bought two of these and both were non-functional, out of the box.

On the first one, the included line was tangled around inside the mechanism. I had to take it apart and unravel about 6 feet of line that was all caught up in the case. It's hard to explain, but it was basically wedged between the outer casing and the internal components, not just in the spool itself.

On the second one, the casting button was completely unseated on one side. The button has two small pegs which pivot inside of holes in the steel case. I had to take the bottom of the case off, bend the steel tabs that hold the pegs in place, reseat the button and bend the tabs back.

Both work great now and all the components seem pretty good, but this company has some serious quality control issues with assembly. It is pretty ridiculous that 2 out of 2 that I ordered were DOA, still sealed in the undamaged factory box. Luckily, I knew how to fix them, but most people who aren't mechanically inclined or perhaps know very little about reels would have had to return both of them. That is really unacceptable.

Still, they are great little reels now and they would be 5 star if not for the time I had to spend on fixing them. If you have some tools and are confident about taking things apart, I wouldn't hesitate to buy one. If not, well, you might be rolling the dice.

Esbit Ultralight Folding Pocket Stove with Six 14g Solid Fuel Tablets steel, Small - Original Used this during a 2 day hike in a cave in the southeastern US. At ambient 58F near ~2,100' AMSL, 1 Esbit 14g fuel tablet just brings 1.5l of water to a boil before burning out. They claim 12 min. burn time. I only observed around 8~9 min, but it did what I needed, was smaller and lighter than propane canisters, etc. Fuzzy guess says the cost per pot heated is similar to propane, with these being a bit more trouble/less flexible, but smaller and lighter.

Compared to Trioxane, these tablets seem to have about ~30% more energy per tablet, but that's just this backpacker's impression. They're harder to light than trioxane, but not overly difficult.

This little stove has a slightly wider base than the old US Army issue Trioxane stoves. This makes balancing a pot on it much easier. Note that canteen cups don't balance well -- it's just a bit too wide for them to fit comfortably. You can sort of jam one in, but it's precarious and falls over if you so much as sneeze at it. This makes sneezing at your canteen cup highly discommended. A great loss, to be sure.

text_fidelity_a:
Dietz #30 Little Wizard Oil Lamp Burning Lantern Blue (Small Tank) Fantastic lantern. If you're used to standard big-box-retailer fare, this lantern is a HUGE step up in quality and size and you'll be very pleasantly surprised. I've burned it ~12 hours and have yet to notice a drop in the fuel level. No smell when burning(except for a few hours after the very first use), even on plain ole kerosene. While it's attractively built and painted, this lantern is clearly built to be used, not just displayed. Packaging was GREAT, I was really surprised at how well this lantern was packaged.

Tips for use: The wick will probably need to be trimmed when you receive it, mine was uneven and had many loose threads. I used angle nippers, a sharp pair of scissors will do better. I just removed the whole burner assembly for easier access and trimmed the wick level with the wick tube. Burn it for several hours the first time OUTSIDE. The paint will be doing it's final outgassing upon being heated and greases and oils from stamping will be burning off during this period, you don't want that going on in your house. When you first light this lantern, turn it up a little bit and let the whole lantern heat up for 10-15 minutes before turning the lantern up to full brightness. Likewise when putting out the lantern, turn it down to a very low flame and let the lantern cool for a few minutes before actually blowing it out. The flame doesn't actually burn liquid fuel, it burns fuel that's vaporized off the wick. If you just blow out the lantern, full throttle to blown out, a bunch of that fuel is still vaporizing off the wick and that smells bad. This can be mitigated considerably by turning down the lantern and letting it cool, which will reduce the amount of fuel that continues to be vaporized after the flame is finally blown out. Odor may be less of an issue with lamp oil, but even with lamp oil, you'll still be inhaling the vaporized lamp oil, even if you're not smelling it. Not healthy.

Now, the one reason I gave 4 stars instead of 5 was that there was a chip down to bare metal on the font when the lantern arrived. As stated above, the packaging was amazing and undamaged, this lantern clearly sustained this chip before being shipped. I used a dab of nailpolish that was fairly close to the color to prevent rust in the future. This did not effect the use of the lantern at all, and I will be buying more.

5/21/16 update: I have several gallons of kerosene through this lantern now. Lantern has performed flawlessly, but I have found that it is actually my least used lantern. It's about the same size, weight, and cost as an Air Pilot, but puts out ~1/2 the light. Yes it burns less fuel, but if you turn down an Air Pilot to the same light level, you'll get about the same fuel consumption while still having the option to turn it up and get more light if you need/want.
text_fidelity_b: Dietz #30 Little Wizard Oil Lamp Burning Lantern Blue (Small Tank)

text_fidelity_a:
Streamlight 88066 Pro Tac Rail Mount HL-X 1000-Lumen Professional Tactical Flashlight with High/Low/Strobe Dual Fuel, Black This is a very well made tac light, very bright and compact. It uses a lithium battery which means it can sit around for years and still be ready when you need it. I like it, but there are a couple things to be aware of, especially for a tactical light, which means something that has to be 100% reliable and ready when you need it.

1) Hitting the mode you want is very tricky. You have to hit the switch just the right number of times (of course) and most tricky at just the right interval. The timing is VERY fast and it is different if you are going to use a particular mode temporarily (light press and hold button) or switching to that mode (press firmly and release staying on that mode). It takes practice, lots of it to hit the mode you want reliably.

2) When the battery runs out, there is absolutely NO WARNING. Either you will click it on and nothing happens or (most of the time) you will click it on and in a few seconds it goes dead. NOT a good situation for a tactical light. The only way this light can be absolutely ready for a critical situation is to put a new fresh $4 battery in it. Battery life isn't great, but that's the price for such a bright light running on a single CR123 battery. Just hope it is ready when you need it. A low battery indicator would be nice.

Still I gave it a soft 4 stars, maybe 3.5 would be more precise. It is a good light if you use it often enough to be good at hitting the right mode and if you have a fresh battery in it.
text_fidelity_b: Streamlight 88066 Pro Tac Rail Mount HL-X 1000-Lumen Professional Tactical Flashlight with High/Low/Strobe Dual Fuel, Black

The most useful items are the anti-bacterial goop and the bandaids.

The card multi-tool could be useful, but ALL the edges are sharp and can easily break skin.

The "tactical knife" is a card-knife that can neither be properly locked open or properly locked closed. It struggled with cutting the plastic this survival kit came wrapped in.

The dust mask is unfinished on the edges. It can easily become unraveled and had lots of loose ends fresh out of the package.

There was a tea candle. Yep.

Compass did not point North. Ever.

Glow sticks were not bright enough to illuminate the desk they were lying right on.

The fire starter is a joke. Don't get me wrong..With some skill it can be used, but it is absolute junk. I broke the metal bar after a few practice tries.

Overall, if I hadn't had a gift card to waste, I would have returned the item for a refund. Even my son who is all about zombie survival thought it was junk.
text_fidelity_b: Citadel Black Zombie Apocalypse Survival Kit - Multi-Tool, Fire Starter, Keyring, Zombie Permit, Stickers, and More

J JACKCUBE DESIGN Skateboard Storage Holder - Skateboard Display Holder, Standing Storage, Skateboard Accessories for Portable Display or Skateboard Parking lot I am not a fan. The construction is simple, 6 total screws, 3 screws per leg. will take anyone, literally, a minute to assemble. Wood looks nice. Construction is sturdy and well made.

My problem:

It doesn't fit my skateboard. It seems to be the wheels. I have larger than I guess the average wheels. nothing ridiculous, a friend told me to get a bit larger diameter to assist in running over cracks/rocks and such while learning. so they have a larger diameter that what the most vanilla build would be. It created a tight fit. I had to really push into it a bit to get the skateboard on there. I could tell the larger size of wheels made the fit tighter. So that's a con, only works with specifically medium to small wheels. Or, perhaps trucks a bit longer. Either way, it requires a level of specificity I don't feel like looking in to.
Edit: Another reviewer mentioned low trucks. I suppose that could also be a cause. To reiterate, the trucks and wheels I am using are right off the shelf at a Zumiez. Standard, vanilla built skateboard, and this thing does not fit it.

I don't understand why the lean. In order to see the graphics of the skateboard, you have to face the stand backwards. So instead of looking at the solid wood design, you are looking at the legs and screws on the backside. Otherwise, you will be looking at the grip tape.

And the lean itself, while not extreme, why? There are less than 10 dollar plastic options that work well enough, and keep the board upright. So with the cheap plastic ones, not only is the board upright, it isn't reliant on trucks/wheel dimensions, and faces the graphics to be visible on display. For a product that is made of better material, I would have expected to be able to do that. The lean is just too awkward for my OCD.

I opted for the cheap 8 dollar plastic solution. Works well enough, board is upright, cool graphic showing, right in the corner of the room.

text_fidelity_a: Coleman OneSource Rechargeable Camping System This flashlight, assembled with battery, weighs 9.6 ounces. It is 7.5 inches long and approximately 2 inches in diameter. The light source is LED. Definitely not a pocket flashlight, but a very good size for camping or just having around the house. It’s quite simple to operate in that it has a single pushbutton that, on the first push, puts it in low mode, second push puts it in high mode, and third push turns it off. The low mode is a quite substantial amount of light in itself, and high mode is a very bright light. The flashlight feels quite nice in the hand. Installing the battery is quite simple as well. You simply put the battery in the back of the flashlight body and twist to align two white dots. The package comes with a USB type-C connector cord for charging. The battery itself has an input for the type-C connector for charging and a standard USB output port that can be used to charge other devices, which is a really cool feature. I like that this rechargeable battery doesn’t need product-specific charger. There is a three light battery charge level indicator on the back of the battery that is operated with a small push button. When the button is held for 2+ seconds, a small LED light comes on, giving you a light on the battery even if when not attached to the flashlight. Again, a really cool feature. Warranty on the battery and the flashlight is 3 years. The battery is part of a multi-product system that utilizes the same battery type for all devices. State Bicycle Offroad Division Megalith Fat Bike got Megalith on 1/5/2015 directly from STATE bikes. used 20% coupon so got bike for $560.
Bike is not worth $700.
IS mounts F & R were hugely off from being perpendicular to Axle centerline.
I had to modify these myself to fix and get decent alignment with the Hayes Prime and 203mm discs I put on immediately.

Bike may work tubeless with the extra heavy CTS tires the bike comes with. However I could not get Vee Missions to work as they fit too loosely on the wheel to hold bead until you can inflate.

I heard from another owner that the stock headset is absolute crap. I noticed the headset myself was bit crappy and fit seemed weird, but have not ridden the bike yet, so i'll take the word of another owner and also upgrade the headset to a Cane Creek Forty
Again. Even though I immediately upgraded parts, the poor quality control of the frame (*disc mounts) has kept me from even being able to ride the bike yet, as I've had to massage it with my 4.5" dewalt grinder

I would be a bit more Annoyed if I had paid the full $700 price. And if I wasn't fabricator with all kinds of tools/welders, I would not have been able to fix some of the issues myself at no cost.
This other owner also told me their is non existant support from STATE. Also if you can't prove it was professionally assembled, he said they will not honor any warranty.
I knew this was a gamble as it's an "internet" only available bike. and also I would be assembling it myself.
I think if I had taken this to a professional bicycle mechanic, they would have laughed and most likely try to sell you another bike, or possibly charge a bit to fix the issues (typically $25 per end, $50 total)

If you plan to upgrade to 1x10 drivetrain, etc, don't waste your money on this bike. Pay more up front and get a better bike that has better components
The only other fairly inexpensive Chromo fatbike I was aware of was Bikesdirect Lurch. Not sure of their quality but wish I had purchased that instead. Surly of course makes chromo bikes but the cost of frame is about what I paid for full Megalith bike (you get what you pay for). Aluminum bikes you have much more options. But it's not just great to play with in the store. I've caught probably 200 trout on mine, and it's been beat up. Dropped, submerged, dragged through mud, and covered in clay. I treated it the same way I did my Abu ProMax, and that piece of garbage died after 2 months.

If you're looking for a great reel and you have $150 to spend, get this and use the extra money to buy a nice rod, some good copoly line, and gas up your truck. Go fish!

The buttons are an issue, reacting in a finicky, frustrating way. My make-do solution is, instead of fumbling with typing in numbers while running, I punch one of the walk-jog-run buttons, which takes me to a given speed. From there, I use the faster-slower button.

Gun Sight Compatible with Salt&Gun 3.0 2.5 2.0 with Manual and Constant Lighting Modes (Gun not Included) This laser comes with six batteries and you only need three so you have one set for backup. The laser itself in my opinion works good and is bright with a thin beam. You can adjust the beam with the included tool. The attached button cord also works good. I could turn it on and off easily and it always worked properly. Mounting the laser was also a non-issue and tightened good.

The problem with this laser is the button switch located on the back cover of the laser. I had a horrible time getting it to work properly. After studying this thing for awhile, I discovered after removing the battery cover that the spring was crooked and would move the batteries out of position. The result was that the spring tension and spring not making center contact was causing the laser to not work properly. The spring was loose and wobbly too. I tried bending it to center but it only made it worse. My husband had spare various size springs in his shop so was able to remake one that fit better. After about an hour of work we finally got it fixed. I had to make sure the spring was dead center when closing the cap so the batteries wouldn't move out of place and had enough tension so when pressing the on/off button it would work. Another little issue is the batteries do not fit perfect inside the case and are a bit wobbly. So there is that.

I hope you have better luck and maybe this was a glitch in the one I received. I really believe the switch could have been designed better. After all, you want the laser to work when you need it. I cannot in all honesty give this item more than 3 stars and I would not recommend it.
